raw_response:
I'm 45, been farming this 3.5 mu plot in Quzhou for 30 years — since I was a teenager helping my father. It's not much land, but it's what feeds my family. Six people at home: my wife, my elderly parents, and two children. My wife and I do most of the farm work, but my older daughter works in a factory in Handan and sends some money back. That helps with cash, but I still watch every yuan. With only 3.5 mu, I can't afford mistakes.

Right now it's spring, and the wheat I planted last October is greening up. I used an improved Jinmai variety, about 25 jin per mu. Before planting, I put down base fertilizer — compound fertilizer with some phosphorus and potassium, plus urea. Now I need to topdress with urea at green-up, about 20 jin per mu. The extension technician told me 15 jin is enough, but I've tried that and the wheat looked yellow by jointing. My soil is sandy loam and doesn't hold nutrients well. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad yield — a bad year means we don't eat well.

I'll irrigate three times for the wheat: once right after topdressing to wash the fertilizer into the soil, once at jointing if it's dry, and once at grain filling. Water from the well is metered now and costs money, but with only 3.5 mu, three times is manageable. Last year we had a dry May and the neighbors who skipped the grain-filling irrigation lost 50 jin per mu. I won't make that mistake.

For weeds in wheat, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring. I don't spray for insects or disease unless I see them — preventive spraying is just throwing money away.

Wheat harvest comes in early June, and then I have maybe 5 to 7 days to get the maize in. It's always a rush. I hire the combine for wheat harvest — about 40 yuan per mu — because there's no other way to finish fast enough. For maize I buy hybrid seed every year, Zhengdan 958 or similar, about 4 jin per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, it won't grow right.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, then topdress urea when the plants are knee-high — around the big trumpet stage. Total nitrogen about 25-26 jin per mu. I'll irrigate twice if needed: once in July if it's dry, and once at tasseling. Maize handles drought better than wheat, so if the rains are decent I might only irrigate once and save the pumping cost.

For maize pesticide, I spray herbicide before emergence. If I see corn borer I'll spray insecticide, but last year it wasn't bad so I'll check first.

Yield? I expect about 420 kg per mu for wheat and around 480 kg per mu for maize if the weather holds. That's what I usually get. I'm not trying to win any yield contests — I need steady production. If I get those numbers, we have enough grain for the family and can sell maybe 1000-1200 kg for cash income.

Total cash costs this year will be around 1,500 yuan — seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, irrigation, and the combine hire. It's a lot for 3.5 mu, but without inputs the yield drops by half. My daughter's remittances cover the input costs, so I can afford it. But I'm still careful. If fertilizer prices jump again, I might cut the maize topdress a little. Wheat comes first — it's the safer crop.
